main_text.p: mæ & officij noftri obliti, & ea tantum quæ molesta nobis, non autem quæ iu- cūda & utilia sunt tum nobis, tum etiam alijs,spectantes, illud ethnicū, λάθε βιώσας [?], sectemur. Neq; enim nobis nati sumus, aut etiam uiuimus, ut integrum nobis sit de nobis ipsis id quod seu dolor, seu fasti- dium rerum præsentium dictat, statuere.
Sint itaque nobis in conspectu hæ gra- uissimæ rationes, quæ monent, quenq; suo loco in honesta societate hominum viuere, & ad extremum usque vitæ spiri- tum perseuerare debere.

1. Quia homo est animal λογικόν [?], ac natura & lege tenetur diligere proximū tanquam seipsum. Dilectionem autem hanc factis, & quidem tota sua vita testa- ri debet: id quod ab eo præstari nequit, si sese subducat è contubernio aliorum hominum. Etsi autem hominum usibus, & mutuis uerę beneficentiæ officijs, contu- bernium eorum seruire debet: principa- lis tamen eius finis est, uerę de Deo doctrinæ studiosa propagatio. Placent sane mihi plurimū hi dulces uersus Stigelij:

p.i: Postquam ubi senserunt se femina ducere cœlo,
Atq; aliquem, mundum qui regat, esse Deum;

page.notes: The Greek words "λάθε βιώσας" and "λογικόν" are hard to read at this resolution: accents and letters are uncertain, so they are marked [?]. The verse line "Post ubi senserunt" is printed as "Poft ubi" with a long s and may be read differently; the first verse line is read as "Postquam ubi" with the word "quam" not clearly visible, so the exact wording of the first verse line is doubtful. The verse is set in italic and is one stanza. Words "seu" and "feu" in the printed text are read as seu. The fragment "mæ" at the start is a continuation from the previous page.
